main_text.p: largiamur ei, animos feparatos esse viatores, cum tamen proprie, & ftricto modo non sint, nec id ab Orientalibus dicatur.

Concludit tandem Hottingerus: Quamquam in Syrorum libris leiturgicis obseruauerim, precibus, ideo potissimum Defunctos Deo commendari, vt tempore vltimi Iudicij clementem refuscitati experiantur Iudicem; gloriosaque adeo beentur resurrectione.

Concludit profecto, verbisque modo imponit finem Hottingerus; Sed si mutare poteft Aethiops pellem suam, aut Pardus varietates suas, & Hottingerus poterit mutare malitiam, cum didicerit malum ab ipsa ineunte aetate. Impofuit finem verbis, sed vtinam fallacijs, vtinam paralogismis. Nam quis Hottingero id inficiatus est, aut inficiatur? An in Ecclesia quoque Romana hoc deprecandi genus pro Defunctis in vsu non sit? & an, qui id praestant, Purgatorium excludant, §& negent? Nequaquam profecto, imo Syri vtrumque deprecandi genus impense pro Defunctis absoluunt, nimirum, vt Deus propitius sit eis tempore vltimi Iudicij, & vt eos liberet a poenis Purgatorijignis. Primum obseruauit probus, ac ingenuus suo more Hottingerus; adeoque probatione non eget; alterius, quod oculos illos Reformato linitos

page.notes: The section mark (§) in the right margin is a printed symbol and is transcribed as a note. The word "beentur" and the run-together "Purgatorijignis" are copied as printed; the scan is clear enough to read them, but they may be printer's errors. The bottom curved line and the dark left edge are scan artefacts and are not transcribed.
